reason: E1 shows computational evidence for chemical clustering and high-temperature SRO in AlxCrCoFeNi, supporting the premise that SRO/clustering can form. However, no cited evidence supports the claimed property enhancements (strength, oxidation, radiation, cryogenic toughness) from SRO, nor the effect of quenching on SRO or properties. E2 and E3 discuss general annealing effects and SRO-property correlations in other HEAs but do not provide specific evidence for the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni system or the claimed property suite.
premises: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs form short-range ordering (SRO) and nanoscale clustering between specific element pairs (e.g., Al–Cr, Al–Fe) during slow cooling.
SRO and clustering enhance high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
Rapid quenching suppresses SRO and clustering formation.
Suppressed SRO/clustering degrades the above properties relative to a slow-cooled baseline.
